present.action: Write down one thing the person actually said and the meaning you added; mark what remains unconfirmed.

action.action: Choose one uncertain point and draft a direct, answerable question; leave room for the person to decline or need time.

findings.before: Ending an exhausted task can free resources for an actual priority.
findings.explanation: Work/career users may not control deadlines, employment terms, or delegated responsibilities. Reflection should support a request or reversible change, not silently assume permission to abandon a task. Existing release checks mention handoffs and should be preserved.
findings.proposedChange: Use scope-aware language: Identify a task that may no longer serve its purpose; check what can end, be reduced, or be handed over before committing its time elsewhere. Apply similar realistic authority checks to work actions that remove obligations.

before: For a creative project, write one established fact beside one open question and identify a way to check that question.
findings.explanation: All 28 aligned cases have identical advice across the three intents. Present needs a reading of existing project conditions; crossroads needs comparable options/unknowns; action needs an experiment. Rust action_refs[topic] and generator scope prefixes cannot express that difference.

proposedChange.implementation: Author relation × topic × intent action and question references, select them in Rust; keep TS a renderer.

present.action: Look at one unfinished section. Separate what the draft already shows from what you are still guessing about its effect.
present.question: Which uncertainty belongs to the work itself, and which comes from not having shown or tested it yet?

crossroads.action: Name two directions for the piece. For each, write what you know from the draft and one unanswered question that could change your choice.
crossroads.question: What would you need to see or hear before preferring one direction?

action.action: Make a rough alternate version of one small section to test a single unanswered question. Compare it with the original before polishing either.
action.question: What did that comparison clarify, and what can remain undecided?

findings.rationale: Different tasks answer different intents while staying grounded in evidence versus uncertainty, not mere lexical variation.

before: The difficulty to account for is using self-criticism as fuel. ... For a creative project, offer one specific form of support with an honest limit on its time or scope.
findings.explanation: The all-reversed Fool/Strength/Death case raises preparation, exhaustion and ending. The advice suddenly makes the user a giver of support. A solo creator need not be supporting anyone. Generic care-boundaries phrasing leaves the object of care unspecified and can pull against the actual spread.

present.action: Name what is sustaining the project and what maintaining it is costing you. Mark one demand that is consuming more attention than the work can repay.
present.question: Which part of caring for this work has become pressure to keep every part alive?

crossroads.action: For each project direction, compare the attention it needs with the time and materials you can actually provide. Name one limit you will protect in either choice.
crossroads.question: Which direction leaves enough capacity to tend the work without treating exhaustion as proof of commitment?

action.action: Give one neglected part of the project a short session, then stop at a limit chosen beforehand. Leave a nonessential demand out of that session.
action.question: What support helped the work, and what demand could stay outside the next session?

findings.rationale: Makes the supported object the project and includes creator capacity; does not infer another person or require more giving.
